sections.title: Designing and planning a cloud solution architecture
sections.description: Business and technical requirements, network, storage and compute choices, migration plans and future improvements

topics.title: 1.1 Designing for business requirements
concepts: Functional and non-functional requirements, business continuity, cost optimization and observability
Workload disposition strategies: build, buy, modify or deprecate
Success measurements such as key performance indicators, return on investment and metrics
topics.examFocus: Start from the business need, then pick the design that meets it. The Well-Architected Framework pillars are the checklist for the trade-offs.
traps: Choosing a product before finding the requirement that decides the design
Treating cost as the only trade-off when reliability, security or performance is the binding constraint

studyQA.question: Which pillars does the exam guide name for the Google Cloud Well-Architected Framework?
studyQA.answer: Operational excellence, security, reliability, performance optimization, cost optimization and sustainability. The guide says they are woven through the exam objectives and should guide architectural decisions.

studyQA.question: What does the cost optimization pillar of the Well-Architected Framework give you?
studyQA.answer: Principles and recommendations to help you optimise the cost of your workloads in Google Cloud.

studyQA.question: What is the Well-Architected Framework for?
studyQA.answer: It gives architectural recommendations and best practices to design a secure, efficient and resilient cloud topology that is optimised for cost, performance and sustainability.

topics.title: 1.2 Designing for technical requirements
concepts: High availability and fail-over design, scalability, performance and latency
Gemini Cloud Assist for designing, deploying, troubleshooting and optimising workloads
Backup and recovery for workloads in Google Cloud and in hybrid environments
topics.examFocus: Match the technical requirement (availability, scale, latency, recovery) to the design choice, and name the pillar the choice serves.
traps: Using one zone for a workload that must stay available when a zone fails
Confusing a backup service with a fail-over design

studyQA.question: What does the reliability pillar help you do?
studyQA.answer: It provides principles and recommendations to design, deploy and manage reliable workloads in Google Cloud.

studyQA.question: What is Gemini Cloud Assist?
studyQA.answer: An AI-powered collaborator that gives agentic guidance for designing, deploying, troubleshooting and optimising workloads, moving teams from reactive troubleshooting towards proactive operations.

studyQA.question: What does Backup and DR provide?
studyQA.answer: Centralised backup and recovery for enterprise workloads running in Google Cloud and in hybrid environments, with policy-based governance.

topics.title: 1.3 Designing network, storage and compute resources
concepts: Cloud-native networking: VPC, peering, firewalls, load balancers, Shared VPC and Private Service Connect
Storage types: object (Cloud Storage), file (Filestore) and databases (Cloud SQL, Spanner, Bigtable, Firestore)
Compute choices: GKE, Cloud Run, Cloud Run functions, Spot VMs and custom machine types
AI infrastructure and models: AI Hypercomputer and Model Garden
topics.examFocus: Read the binding constraint: who must control the network, whether the data is objects, files or rows, and how much control the team needs over orchestration.
traps: Picking GKE when the team only needs to run a container and has no need for Kubernetes control
Using VPC peering when one central team must own the network, which is the Shared VPC case
Choosing a single-region relational database when the requirement is global scale

studyQA.question: How do Shared VPC and VPC Network Peering differ?
studyQA.answer: Shared VPC connects resources from several projects to one common VPC network that a host project administers centrally. VPC Network Peering connects two separately administered VPC networks so their resources can talk over internal IP addresses.

studyQA.question: What does Private Service Connect let consumers do?
studyQA.answer: It lets consumers access managed services privately from inside their own VPC network.

studyQA.question: When does Cloud Run fit better than GKE?
studyQA.answer: Cloud Run is a fully managed platform for running code, a function or a container, so it fits when you want to deploy without managing a cluster. GKE is a managed Kubernetes service, which fits when you need the Kubernetes API and control over orchestration.

studyQA.question: What are Spot VMs good for?
studyQA.answer: Spot VMs are excess Compute Engine capacity at large discounts, and Google may preempt them to reclaim capacity, so they suit fault-tolerant workloads such as batch jobs.

studyQA.question: What is a custom machine type?
studyQA.answer: A Compute Engine VM with your own number of vCPUs and amount of memory, for when no predefined machine type fits.

studyQA.question: Which storage service holds unstructured objects with high durability?
studyQA.answer: Cloud Storage lets you store, manage and retrieve unstructured data with high durability and global availability.

topics.title: 1.4 Creating a migration plan
concepts: Assessing systems and data, then migrating them with Google Cloud Migration Center
Migration methodologies, workload testing, network planning and dependency planning
Software licence implications and financial impact
topics.examFocus: A migration plan starts with discovery and assessment, including cost estimates, before any workload moves.
traps: Moving workloads before discovering their dependencies
Ignoring licence terms when estimating the cost of the move

studyQA.question: What does Migration Center help you do?
studyQA.answer: It is a unified platform that accelerates your journey to Google Cloud. It estimates cloud costs, discovers and assesses your assets, and provides tooling for different migration scenarios, without changing your workloads.

studyQA.question: What does Database Migration Service migrate?
studyQA.answer: Data and metadata from a source database to a destination database, supporting migrations to Cloud SQL and AlloyDB for PostgreSQL.

topics.title: 1.5 Envisioning future solution improvements
concepts: Cloud and technology improvements, and the evolution of business needs
topics.examFocus: Expect scenarios where a design must keep working as needs change. Use the framework pillars to judge a proposed improvement.
traps: Designing only for today's load with no room for the business to grow

studyQA.question: Which framework does the exam guide call a key requirement for the role?
studyQA.answer: Familiarity with the Google Cloud Well-Architected Framework, whose pillars should guide architectural decisions.

questions.question: A central network team must own one VPC network, its subnets and its firewall rules, while many project teams launch VMs into it. Which design fits?
options: VPC Network Peering between a network in every project
Shared VPC with a host project and service projects
Private Service Connect endpoints in every project
Cloud VPN tunnels between the projects
questions.explanation: Shared VPC connects resources from several projects to one common VPC network administered in a host project, so network control stays central.
whyOthersWrong: Peering connects separately administered networks, so each team would still run its own network.
Private Service Connect publishes and reaches a service privately; it does not share one network among projects.
Cloud VPN joins networks through encrypted tunnels; it does not give one team central control of a shared network.

questions.question: Two business units each run their own VPC network and must keep administering it themselves, but their VMs need to talk over internal IP addresses. What should the architect recommend?
options: A single project for both units
questions.explanation: VPC Network Peering connects two VPC networks so their resources communicate over internal IP addresses, and each network stays administered separately.
whyOthersWrong: Shared VPC hands network administration to a central host project, which the units do not want.
Merging into one project removes the separation the units want to keep.
A load balancer distributes traffic across instances; it does not connect two networks.

questions.question: A team has a containerised API and no Kubernetes expertise. It wants to deploy the image and let Google handle servers and scaling. Which platform fits?
options: Compute Engine with a managed instance group
questions.explanation: Cloud Run is a fully managed platform for running code, a function or a container on Google's scalable infrastructure, with no cluster to manage.
whyOthersWrong: GKE Standard gives Kubernetes control, which this team neither needs nor has the skills for.
A managed instance group of VMs leaves the team managing machines and images.
Filestore is a managed file server, not a compute platform.

questions.question: A media company renders video overnight. Jobs can restart safely and the company wants the lowest compute price, accepting that capacity may be reclaimed. What should it use?
questions.explanation: Spot VMs are excess Compute Engine capacity at large discounts that Google may preempt, which suits fault-tolerant batch work.
whyOthersWrong: Custom machine types change a VM's shape, not its price model or preemption behaviour.
A standard on-demand VM is not discounted for fault-tolerant work.
Functions respond to events; they are not the discounted compute for long batch rendering.

questions.question: A legacy application needs 6 vCPUs and 40 GB of memory, and no predefined machine type matches. What is the best way to avoid paying for unused resources?
options: Choose the next larger predefined machine type
Create the VM with a custom machine type
Move the application to Cloud Storage
questions.explanation: A custom machine type lets you choose your own number of vCPUs and amount of memory when predefined types do not fit.
whyOthersWrong: A larger predefined type pays for unused vCPUs and memory.
Spot VMs change the price and the availability, not the machine shape.
Cloud Storage holds objects; it does not run applications.

questions.question: A global payments platform needs a relational database with strongly consistent transactions, virtually unlimited scale and no maintenance windows. Which database should the architect choose?
questions.explanation: Spanner combines relational capabilities with virtually unlimited scale and no maintenance windows.
whyOthersWrong: Cloud SQL is a managed engine for MySQL, PostgreSQL and SQL Server, without the global scale requirement.
Bigtable is a wide-column table for single-keyed data, not a relational database.
Firestore is a document database, not a relational one.

questions.question: An advertising firm ingests billions of events keyed by a single row key and reads them by that key at very high throughput. Which storage fits best?
questions.explanation: Bigtable is a sparsely populated table that scales to billions of rows and thousands of columns for single-keyed data.
whyOthersWrong: Cloud SQL is a relational service, not built for billions of key-addressed rows.
Filestore is a shared file server and does not suit key-based lookups at that scale.
BigQuery analyses data with SQL; it is not the store for key-based reads at high throughput.

questions.question: A render farm of VMs needs one shared file system that every machine can mount. Which service fits?
questions.explanation: Filestore provides fully managed file servers that VMs and other clients can mount.
whyOthersWrong: Cloud Storage is object storage, not a mountable file system with file semantics.
Bigtable is a table store, not a file system.
Spanner is a database, not a file server.

questions.question: A team must build a pipeline that processes both streams and batches with the same Apache Beam code, using a managed service. What should it use?
questions.explanation: Dataflow provides unified stream and batch data processing at scale and uses Apache Beam.
whyOthersWrong: Managed Service for Apache Spark runs Spark and other open source tools on clusters; the requirement here is Beam code.
Cloud Storage stores objects and does not process data.
Cloud Build runs software builds, not data pipelines.

questions.question: A software vendor publishes a managed service and wants customers to reach it privately from inside their own VPC networks, without joining whole networks together. What should the vendor use?
questions.explanation: Private Service Connect lets consumers access managed services privately from inside their own VPC network.
whyOthersWrong: Shared VPC shares one network across projects of one organisation; it does not publish a service to customers.
Cloud Armor protects against DDoS and web attacks; it does not provide private connectivity.
Peering connects two whole networks, which the vendor wants to avoid.

questions.question: A company plans to move hundreds of on-premises servers. What should it do first, using Google Cloud tooling?
options: Discover and assess the assets and estimate the cost in Migration Center
Copy every server to Spot VMs
Create a Cloud Run service per server
Deploy Cloud Armor in front of the data centre
questions.explanation: Migration Center estimates cloud costs, discovers and assesses assets and plans the move without changing workloads.
whyOthersWrong: Moving first, without assessment, ignores dependencies and costs.
Cloud Run is a platform for containers and functions, not a method to move servers as they are.
Cloud Armor protects Google Cloud deployments; it does not help plan a move.

questions.question: A team must move a running PostgreSQL database into Cloud SQL with a managed tool that migrates data and metadata. Which service fits?
questions.explanation: Database Migration Service migrates data and metadata from a source database to a destination such as Cloud SQL or AlloyDB for PostgreSQL.
whyOthersWrong: Storage Transfer Service moves object and file data between storage systems, not live databases.
Dataflow builds data pipelines; it is not a database migration tool.
Backup and DR protects workloads with backups; it does not migrate a database into another service.

questions.question: A bank wants centralised, policy-based backup and recovery for VMs, databases and hybrid workloads in one managed service. Which service should it choose?
questions.explanation: Backup and DR is a managed service for centralised backup and recovery of enterprise workloads in Google Cloud and hybrid environments, with policy-based governance.
whyOthersWrong: Cloud Storage stores objects; it is not a policy-based backup service for many workload types.
Filestore is a file server, not a backup service.
Cloud Monitoring collects metrics; it does not back up workloads.

questions.question: An architecture board wants one Google source of principles covering reliability, security, cost, performance, sustainability and operational excellence before approving a design. What should the architects use?
questions.explanation: The Google Cloud Well-Architected Framework gives recommendations and best practices across its pillars for designing secure, efficient and resilient cloud topologies.
whyOthersWrong: Migration Center helps assess and plan a move; it is not a set of design principles.
Budgets set spend alerts; they do not cover design principles.
Model Garden is a library of AI models.

questions.question: An on-call engineer wants an AI collaborator in Google Cloud that helps troubleshoot an outage and suggests how to optimise the affected workload. What should the team use?
questions.explanation: Gemini Cloud Assist is an AI-powered collaborator that gives agentic guidance for designing, deploying, troubleshooting and optimising workloads.
whyOthersWrong: Cloud Trace shows request latency; it is not an AI assistant that guides troubleshooting and optimisation.
Spot VMs are discounted, preemptible compute.
Binary Authorization enforces which container images may deploy.
